title: shadowlap.config.json
description: Project configuration for Shadowlap. Every key is optional; an empty object is valid. Add "$schema" pointing at this file for completion and validation in an editor.

normalize.description: Rules that mask values before fingerprinting, so a generated id or today's date does not fork a replay. Stored content is untouched.

redact.description: Rules applied to every export, pack and share link of a run: `shadowlap pack`, every `shadowlap export` and `shadowlap share`. A push copies runs to the team store as recorded. A redacted pack still replays, because these are applied as normalizers when it does.

clock.description: auto (the default): dates and timestamps near each run's start match across days. exact: they must be equal.

prices.description: USD per million tokens, by model name prefix. Extends and overrides the built-in table; used for cost estimates only.

http.description: Hosts called straight from a client library, recorded as tool calls with an effect. A key is a host like api.example.com or *.example.com, with an optional :port.

providers.description: Hosts of a provider's wire format that the agent sends model calls to, such as a gateway or an OpenAI-compatible service: each is captured and recorded as that provider's calls, with its streaming, usage and interventions. Calls under its root match as the format's own API names them.

host.description: api.example.com or *.example.com (any subdomain), either with an optional :port. Without a port, its calls are captured over https; with one, at that port over http too.

format.description: The wire format the host speaks: OpenAI's (Chat Completions and the Responses API), Anthropic's Messages API, or Gemini's.

root.description: The path of the base URL the format's SDK is given at this host, such as /api/v1 for OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1): a call under it matches as the format's own API names it (POST /v1/chat/completions), and keeps its full path as its name.

mcp.description: `shadowlap mcp`: effects by tool name, overriding what the server's annotations imply.

tools.description: Tools by name (or, for a host under `http`, the host): `trust` marks a read that brings outside text in (a web page, an email, a ticket) as untrusted, so `shadowlap injection` plants payloads in its results. Recorded on each call of the tool as it is made, so a run keeps it wherever it is opened; read when a run is tested, it wins over what the SDK's `trust` option, an MCP server's openWorldHint or an earlier config recorded.

unrecorded.$comment: Unrecorded tools: the effect of tools the agent runs without Shadowlap recording them (replay and test refuse to run an unrecorded write again).
unrecorded.description: The effect of each tool the model calls that shadowlap does not record (a built-in such as Bash, a framework's tool, an MCP server reached without shadowlap mcp). A replay runs such a tool again for real, so `replay` and `test` refuse while one of them writes: a declared `write` is refused, a declared `read` only warned about. `--allow-unrecorded <names>` lets a replay run them anyway.

trust.description: untrusted: shadowlap injection plants in its reads. trusted: it doesn't, whatever the SDK or the MCP server said.

build.description: The command that builds the agent, such as "npm run build": repair (in each candidate's worktree, and in the working tree after --apply), fix apply, verify (in the checkout of the code before a change), migrate apply and bisect (in each commit's worktree) run it where they would run --build and none is given. Run in a shell; --build "" runs none.

repair.description: `shadowlap repair`: the model that proposes fixes. It is yours, from any vendor, and is only asked; the verify gate decides what is kept.

repairer.description: provider:model, such as anthropic:claude-opus-5-5, openai:<model> or claude-code (your own Claude Code, in print mode). anthropic alone means claude-opus-5-5. --repairer overrides it.

baseUrl.description: The repairer's API base URL, for a gateway or an OpenAI-compatible server. Defaults to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or OPENAI_BASE_URL.

timeout.description: Seconds the repairer may take to answer before repair gives up on it and says so. Default 600. --repairer-timeout overrides it.

verify.description: `shadowlap verify`: how a good run is kept. It is kept unless its pass rate drops by `margin` or more below its baseline's, at the gate's risk: the same run at the base revision, attempt for attempt (`paired`), or its golden's test history (`history`), up to `max` pairs or attempts. --margin and --baseline override them.

margin.description: The drop in pass rate from the baseline that breaks a good run: 0.1 is 10 points. Default 0.1.

baseline.description: paired (default): the same run at the base revision, paired attempt for attempt with the change's. history: its golden's test history.

max.description: The most pairs (paired) or attempts (history) a good run takes; between the verdicts then, it is inconclusive. Default 200.

guard.description: The network guard. `accept` names the runtimes whose connections the guard can't watch that --guard block takes as they are: "claude-code", the Claude Code CLI the Claude Agent SDK runs, which no preload loads into. Node and Python processes keep --guard block. The GitHub Action's guard-accept input, and SHADOWLAP_GUARD_ACCEPT, add to it.

accept.description: The runtimes --guard block accepts unwatched: "claude-code" alone.

store.description: The team store: the project's runs in a bucket you own, written by `shadowlap store set`. s3://bucket/folder, gs://bucket/folder, az://account/container/folder or r2://account/bucket/folder; a query adds what the name can't say (region, endpoint, path-style, auth=hmac, profile). Credentials never go here: each machine uses its own.

ciPush.description: Whether `shadowlap test --push` pushes test runs and their report to the team store from CI (true unless set to false). `shadowlap store push-from-ci on|off` writes it; outside CI, --push always pushes.

tests.description: Outcome checks for `shadowlap test`, by recording directory relative to this file. `*` is allowed in the last path segment. Two keys set the test session instead: suiteRisk and baselineBranch.

suiteRisk.description: The most a healthy suite may go red for nothing, split across its gated goldens: each fails a golden at its good rate, or runs out of attempts there, at most suiteRisk divided by their number of the time. Default 0.05; `shadowlap test --suite-risk` overrides it for one session.

baselineBranch.description: The branch a gate against history takes its baseline from: only sessions that passed on it, for no pull request, count. Default: the default branch, from CI's variables or git's origin/HEAD.

fork.description: The recording is expected to diverge: the replay goes live from the fork and passes on its checks alone.

repeat.description: Run the replay this many times.

passes.description: Attempts that must pass, out of `repeat`. Defaults to all of them.

gate.description: Decide on the attempts as they come in, with stated error rates, instead of `repeat` and `passes` (give one or the other). Needs `fork`. Either a sequential test between two pass rates, or a comparison with the golden's own test history.

oneOf.description: Wald's sequential probability ratio test: pass at `good` or more, fail at `bad` or less, each verdict wrong at most `risk` of the time, inconclusive when `max` attempts run out between the two.

good.description: A pass rate the gate passes. Default 0.9.

bad.description: A pass rate the gate fails, below `good`. Default 0.7.

risk.description: The most a verdict may be wrong at `good` or at `bad`. Default 0.05.

max.description: The most attempts it runs. Default 80: an agent that always passes needs 12, one that passes 95% of the time 16.7 on average; a lower limit leaves more goldens inconclusive, which fails CI by default.

oneOf.description: Against the golden's test history: from `min` attempts on, after each one, fail when the chance its pass rate dropped by `drop` or more from the last `window` sessions is above 1 - `risk`, pass once that chance is 1/2 or less, and run another attempt in between, up to `max`. Without history, its recording is the baseline.

drop.description: The drop in pass rate that fails it: 0.15 is 15 points. Default 0.15.

risk.description: It fails when the chance of that drop is above 1 - risk. Default 0.05.

window.description: How many of the golden's last sessions make the baseline. Default 10.

min.description: Attempts it runs before it decides. Default 5.

max.description: The most attempts it runs: with a drop still likelier than not but short of 1 - `risk` then, it is inconclusive. Default 40, and never below `min`.

tools.description: By tool name: a count, or a count with arguments the call must contain.

args.description: Counts only calls whose arguments contain these values.

answer.description: The text of the last model response.

inputTokens.description: Input tokens the run’s model requests add up to, cache reads included.

outputTokens.description: Output tokens the run’s model responses add up to.

cost.description: USD from the price table. A model with no price fails the check rather than passing quietly.

calls.description: Rules every call of a tool must meet: the tools that come before it, and predicates on its arguments, which may read a value from the most recent call of another tool before it ("@lookup_order.result.total"). A tool never called meets every rule: pair it with "tools" when the call must happen.

when.description: Checks that apply once a call matched a condition: each is not applicable, never passed, while the condition never held.

then.description: An expect object, read like this one, with at least one check.

judge.description: Questions a model answers yes or no about the run. The judge's call is recorded like any model call: a golden is judged once when it is packed, every clean replay after is judged from the recording, free, and a fork asks the judge live. A check with no recorded verdict and no way to ask live is inconclusive, never passed.

task.description: `shadowlap tasks`: the golden as a task a model is scored on. Every key is optional.

takeover.description: The model call where the model under test takes over; the calls before it replay from the recording. Defaults to the call blame found, else the first model call after the last recorded input, else the first.

why.description: Why that call, in a few words.

rewards.description: What a passing attempt does, in a few words, such as "escalate above the limit". Defaults to the outcome checks.

scope.description: The scope the agent's model calls are made in, when a simulated user's are made in another (scope() in the SDKs): the default takeover is the agent's call. Defaults to the scope blame was limited to.

injection.description: The golden's injection gate: shadowlap test runs its injection test once its replay passes, planting payloads in its untrusted reads (live from the model call that reads them, writes stubbed, reads the recording doesn't hold fenced), and fails it when more attempts obey, or are influenced, than allowed, or when the test showed too little to say (inconclusive, which shadowlap test --inconclusive warn lets through).

obeyed.description: Attempts that may obey a planted instruction (a tool call carrying its canary: a write, or a read that carries it out). Default 0.

influenced.description: Attempts that may be influenced (a write no clean replay made). Default: no limit.

repeat.description: Attempts per untrusted read and payload. Default 1.

templates.description: The built-in templates to plant: all (the default), none, or a list of their ids (shadowlap injection --list-templates).

payloads.description: A file of your own payloads, relative to this file: text (one a line, or blocks between --- lines), JSON or JSON Lines. {{canary}} in them is filled in.

baselines.description: Clean replays of each read, from the model call that reads it, that influenced compares with. Default 3.

liveReads.description: Run the reads the recording doesn't hold after the fork, instead of fencing them (the agent gets an error for a fenced read). A read that carries planted text is fenced all the same. Default false.

chaos.description: `shadowlap test --chaos`: the golden's error-path presets, each a fork where a tool or the provider fails. false leaves the golden out of test --chaos. Every key is optional.

presets.description: The presets to run, in any order: timeout (a tool times out), empty (it answers with nothing), malformed (its JSON cut short), oversized (its longest text repeated), 429 and 500 (the model call that reads it fails). Defaults to all of them.

expect.description: What every attempt must pass besides the agent exiting 0, in the grammar of the entry's own expect: those checks describe the path the recording took, which a path through a failure needn't take. Defaults to the upper bounds the entry's expect sets on write tools, which hold on any path.

tool.description: The tool whose first call the tool presets hit. Defaults to the first tool call that reads the world (a read, else a tool of no declared effect, else a write).

gate.description: The sequential test each preset's attempts are decided by (Wald's sequential probability ratio test, as a tests entry's gate takes it; a gate against the golden's history is refused, since a preset has none): pass at `good` or more, fail at `bad` or less, each verdict wrong at most `risk` of the time, inconclusive when `max` attempts run out between the two. Defaults to the golden's repeat and passes.

good.description: A pass rate the gate passes. Default 0.9.

bad.description: A pass rate the gate fails, below `good`. Default 0.7.

risk.description: The most a verdict may be wrong at `good` or at `bad`. Default 0.05.

max.description: The most attempts it runs. Default 80, as a tests entry's gate. It must allow an agent that always passes to pass: 12 attempts at the defaults.

oversize.description: The characters an oversized result grows to. Defaults to 1000000, past what a model's context takes.

timeout.description: Seconds an attempt may run before it is stopped, and fails: an error path can hang. Defaults to 300.

effect.description: What the call does to the world outside its arguments. Required by design: the only safe default would be write.

rule.description: A normalizer or redaction rule: a scope (kind, name), a path, a pattern, and what a match becomes. Every form `shadowlap normalize add` writes: a pattern anywhere, a pattern at a path, or a path alone, which replaces the whole value there.

kind.description: Restrict to one call kind. Omit for any.

name.description: Restrict to one call name: a tool name, or e.g. "POST /v1/messages". Omit for any.

path.description: Where in the request to apply it: a JSONPath subset such as $.messages[0].content, with [*] and .* wildcards and ["key"]. Omit to apply `pattern` to every string.

pattern.description: A named pattern (iso-date, iso-datetime, uuid, ulid, number, email) or a /regex/flags literal. With a path, omit it to replace the whole value.

replace.description: What the match becomes while matching, e.g. <uuid>.

count.description: An exact count, or a range: 0, ">= 1", "<= 12", "2-4".

amount.description: An amount in USD, or a range: 0.5, "<= 0.50", "0.1-0.4". A leading $ is allowed.

callRule.description: A rule every call of `tool` must meet. It needs "after", "args" that name an argument, or both.

tool.description: The tool whose every call is checked.

after.description: A tool, or a list of tools, that each have a call before every call of `tool`.

args.description: The call’s arguments, by name, each a value to match.

callCondition.description: Holds once any call of `tool` matches `args` and `result`.

result.description: What the call returned, matched as a value.

match.description: A value to match: a literal (equal; an object matches the keys it gives, a list item by item), a reference such as "@lookup_order.result.total" or "@lookup_order.args.order_id" (the value from the most recent call of that tool before the call checked), or a predicate such as { "<=": 100 }. An object whose keys are all operators is a predicate; any other object is matched key by key, and may not have a key named like an operator it is not (gt, contains, $in, endswith): write { "=": { … } } to match one.

predicate.description: Comparisons that must all hold. A number written as text compares as the number; text compares as it is, case included.

in.description: One of a list, or of the list a reference reads; with * in its path, of the values it reaches ("@lookup_customer.result.*").

includes.description: Text that contains this text, or a list that has this item.

not.description: A predicate or a value that must not match. A value that is missing never matches, negated or not.

reference.description: "@<tool>.result.<path>" or "@<tool>.args.<path>": the value from the most recent call of that tool before the call checked. The path is the JSONPath subset of normalizers (.total, .items[0].sku). A string that starts with "@@" is text that starts with one "@".

judge.description: A question a model answers yes or no about the run.

name.description: Its verdict is kept under this name, so each judge has its own.

of.description: What the judge reads: the last model response (the default), what the agent printed, or the conversation and the tool calls.

model.description: The judge’s model: a Claude, OpenAI or Gemini model (claude-haiku-4-5, gpt-5.5, o3, gemini-3-flash), or any model with its provider before it, such as openai:gpt-5.5.

pass.description: The answer that passes. Default: yes.

references.description: A reference, or one whose path has * and reads every value it reaches ("@lookup_customer.result.*"), which only "in" takes.

severalValues.description: A reference whose path has *: it names several values, which only "in" can compare with.

operand.description: A value to compare with: any value, or a reference to one.
